blogs.title: Triple Trouble: Navigating the Anatomy of a TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV Procedure
blogs.description: An in-depth technical breakdown of the 'triple-stent' challenge. This post explores the unique geometric constraints of placing a third valve inside two existing transcatheter frames, analyzing how frame overlap reduces the effective orifice area (EOA), increases the risk of patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM), and complicates commissural alignment. We will dissect the specific procedural choices made in this case, such as high implantation strategies and balloon post-dilation techniques used to maximize flow in a crowded annulus.

blogs.title: To Re-Treat or Not? Managing Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis After Multiple TAVIs
blogs.description: A critical discussion on the therapeutic dilemma of treating infective endocarditis (IE) in patients with multiple prior TAVI implants. We examine the ESC guidelines regarding surgery versus catheter intervention for Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis (PVE), specifically focusing on the 'window of opportunity' after antibiotic cure. This post analyzes why this patient was deemed a candidate for a third transcatheter intervention despite a history of *Enterococcus faecalis* IE, emphasizing the rigorous imaging criteria (absence of vegetations, negative cultures) required to safely bypass open-heart surgery.

blogs.title: The Coronary Minefield: Preventing Obstruction in Sequential Transcatheter Reinterventions
blogs.description: Focusing on one of the most feared complications in serial TAVI: coronary artery obstruction. This educational piece details how pre-procedural CT planning becomes exponentially more difficult with every added valve layer. We review the specific metrics measured in this case (coronary ostial height, sinus dimensions, valve-to-coronary distance) and discuss strategic maneuvers like commissural alignment and supra-annular deployment designed to create a 'neo-skirt' gap sufficient to maintain coronary patency and future access.

blogs.title: Beyond Survival: The Imperative for Lifetime Planning in Structural Heart Disease
blogs.description: Moving beyond acute procedural success, this post addresses the concept of 'lifetime management' for structural heart disease. Using this case study, we argue that decisions made during a primary TAVI must anticipate potential future failures and re-interventions. We discuss the trade-offs between current valve types (e.g., Lotus vs. Evolut vs. Acurate) and how early discussions about surgical risk profiles and anatomical constraints can dictate whether a patient remains eligible for future catheter-based solutions or is forced into prohibitive surgical territory later.
